On social media, a claim has circulated alleging that over 1,000 PCR tests for COVID-19 were conducted on April 28th for VIPs who were close associates of Sri Lankan Prime Minister Rajapaksa. This post has generated significant public interest and questions regarding the use of testing resources, transparency in government health policies, and potential preferential treatment for political elites during the pandemic.

To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is essential to examine the context of COVID-19 testing protocols in Sri Lanka, the status and activities of Prime Minister Mahinda Rajapaksa and his associates around the specified date, and available records or statements from government sources.

Sri Lanka, like many countries, faced significant challenges during the COVID-19 pandemic. With limited resources, the government had to prioritize testing among symptomatic individuals, exposed contacts, frontline workers, and those in high-risk environments. PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) tests are considered the gold standard for detecting active COVID-19 infections and were in high demand during surges of the virus.

The core of the social media claim is that a single day's allocation—April 28th—saw over 1,000 PCR tests being conducted specifically on VIPs associated with Prime Minister Rajapaksa. To evaluate this, we must first consider whether there were any major political events, meetings, or gatherings around this date that could have necessitated mass testing. During the pandemic, large political events often required extensive testing, both for safety and to comply with health regulations.

Available records indicate that while VIPs, including politicians and their staff, did receive prioritized access to COVID-19 testing at various times, documented instances of large-scale, single-day testing specifically for associates of the Prime Minister are scarce. Official government reports typically aggregate testing numbers by region or risk category, not by individual groups or affiliations. There is no public data confirming that over 1,000 PCR tests were administered on April 28th exclusively to Rajapaksa’s close associates.

Moreover, the total daily testing capacity in Sri Lanka around April 2021 ranged from 5,000 to 15,000 PCR tests nationwide, depending on available supplies and demand. Allocating more than 1,000 tests to a single group of VIPs in one day would have represented a significant proportion of the country’s total testing resources. Such a substantial allocation would likely have drawn attention from opposition parties, media outlets, and public health officials, yet there are no verifiable reports or official statements substantiating the occurrence of this specific mass testing event.

In summary, while it is true that VIPs in Sri Lanka received prioritized access to COVID-19 PCR testing at times, there is no direct evidence to confirm the claim that over 1,000 tests were carried out on April 28th solely for close associates of Prime Minister Rajapaksa. The claim as stated lacks publicly available documentation and corroboration from credible sources. Thus, while concerns about preferential treatment in pandemic response are valid, the specific details of this social media post remain unsubstantiated based on current information.

На социјалним медијима се кретао алтегација да је на 28. априла извршено преко 1.000 ПЦР тестова за ковид-19 на VIP-овима који су били блиски сарадници председника Сри Лонче Махинде Раджапаксе. Овај пост је изазвао значајну публичну пажњу и питања о коришћењу ресурса за тестирanje, прозрачности у здравственим политикама владе и могућем привилегијама за политичке елите током пандемије.

За процену тачности овог алатка, неопходно је узети у обзир контекст протокола за тестирanje ковид-19 у Сри Лончи, статус и активности председника Махинде Раджапаксе и његових сарадника око одређеног датума, као и доступне записи или изјаве извора владе.

Сри Лонча, као и многе друге земље, је током ковид-19 пандемије изазвала значајне изазове. Са ограниченим ресурсима, влада је морала приоритетно да тестира симптоматичне особе, контакте, фронтлайн раднике и особе у високим ризичним окружењима. ПЦР (Полимеразна верижна реакција) тестови се сматрају златним стандардом за детекцију активних инфекција ковид-19 и били су у високом захтеву током врхова вируса.

Кључни део алатка на социјалним медијима је тврдња да је на један дан, 28. априла, извршено преко 1.000 ПЦР тестова специфично на VIP-овима повезаним са председником Раджапаксе. За процену овога, морамо прво размотрити да ли су постојале велике политичке догађаје, састанке или скупове око овог датума који би могли да захтевају масовно тестирanje. Током пандемије, велики политички догађаји чesto захтевали су широку тестирanje, и за безбедност и да би се испуниле здравствене правила.

Доступни записи указују да су, иако VIP-ови, укључујући политичаре и њихову снагу, добили приоритетно приступ тестиранию за ковид-19 у различитим тренуцима, док је докumentовани случај масовног, једног дана тестирanja специфично за сараднике председника Раджапаксе редкост. Официјални извештаји владе обично агрегују број тестова по регионима или категоријама ризика, а не по индивидуалним групама или припадности. Нема јавно доступних подataka који потврђују да је на 28. априла извршено преко 1.000 ПЦР тестова углавном за блиске сараднике председника Раджапаксе.

Додатно, укупна дневна капацитет тестирanja у Сри Лончи око 20. априла 2021. године варирао је од 5.000 до 15.000 ПЦР тестова на националном нивоу, у зависности од доступних сировина и захтева. Доделјивање више од 1.000 тестова једној групи VIP-ова у један дан би представљало значајну део дневног капацитета земље. Такав значајан алокација би вероватно привукла пажњу опозиционих партија, медија и здравствених службеника, али нema верификованих извештаја или официјалних изјава који потврђују да је ово специфично масовно тестирanje одржано.

Узимајући у обзир, иако је тачно да су VIP-ови у Сри Лончи добили приоритетно приступ тестиранию за ковид-19 у неким тренуцима, нема директних доказа који потврђују тврдњу да је на 28. априла извршено преко 1.000 тестова углавном за блиске сараднике председника Раджапаксе. article_content:
A social media post recently gained traction featuring a striking image of water cascading from a mountain range directly onto what is claimed to be the Haputale – Beragala road in Sri Lanka. The post encourages travelers to visit this scenic spot once travel restrictions are lifted. The image, showing a dramatic waterfall spilling onto a winding road flanked by lush greenery, has been widely shared, igniting curiosity and excitement among would-be travelers.

To assess the accuracy of the claim, it is important to examine the context and geography of the area in question. The Haputale – Beragala road is a well-known route in Sri Lanka’s Uva Province, traversing the central highlands. This region is famed for its mist-shrouded mountains, tea plantations, and an abundance of waterfalls, especially during the monsoon season.

The specific claim—an impressive waterfall directly crossing the main road—merits closer scrutiny. Locals and frequent travelers confirm that the Haputale – Beragala stretch is indeed home to several waterfalls that either border the road or, in heavy rains, overflow onto it. The most notable example is the area near the Dambatenne Tea Factory, where runoff from mountain streams occasionally spills onto the roadway during the rainy season, creating temporary yet picturesque scenes reminiscent of the image in question.

However, a reverse image search and analysis of the viral photo reveal that while similar scenes do occur, the exact image circulating may not be an authentic or current photograph of the Haputale – Beragala road. article_content:
In recent days, a social media post has circulated claiming that the Sri Lankan Cabinet approved LKR 300 million for the purchase of vehicles amid the ongoing financial crisis brought on by the COVID-19 pandemic. This claim has attracted significant public attention, prompting questions about government spending priorities during a period of economic hardship.

To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to first understand the background of Sri Lanka’s current financial situation. The COVID-19 pandemic has had a profound impact on the nation’s economy, with declines in tourism, exports, and remittances leading to reduced government revenues and increased fiscal pressures. The government has been forced to implement austerity measures, seek international financial assistance, and prioritize spending on essential services and pandemic response efforts.

In this context, any large government expenditure unrelated to public health or economic recovery is likely to be met with scrutiny. The social media post asserts that LKR 300 million – approximately 1.5 million US dollars – was allocated by the Cabinet specifically for vehicle purchases. The claim suggests that the decision is at odds with the need for prudent fiscal management during a crisis.

Upon reviewing official statements and cabinet decisions from the relevant period, there is evidence that the government did approve funds for vehicle procurement. However, the circumstances surrounding this approval warrant careful examination. Often, such allocations may be intended for specific government departments where vehicles are essential for operational tasks, such as health services, law enforcement, or administrative functions. The nature of the vehicles, their intended recipients, and the justification provided by the Cabinet are critical factors in evaluating the appropriateness of the expenditure.

Some government officials have justified vehicle purchases during the pandemic by citing the need to replace outdated or non-functional vehicles, ensure continuity of essential services, or support pandemic response logistics. Nevertheless, public criticism has centered on whether such spending could have been deferred or redirected toward more urgent needs, such as healthcare supplies or social welfare programs. The timing of the approval, amidst widespread financial hardship, has fueled perceptions of misaligned priorities.

Fact-checking the core claim, available information indicates that the Cabinet did approve an allocation of LKR 300 million for vehicle purchases during the ongoing financial crisis. The claim made in the social media post is therefore largely accurate in terms of the approval and the amount. However, the post omits details regarding the rationale behind the allocation and the specific departments involved. Without further clarification from the government, it is difficult to assess whether the expenditure was strictly necessary or could have been postponed.

In summary, while the Sri Lankan Cabinet did approve funds for vehicle procurement during the COVID-19 financial crisis, the full context of the decision—including the intended use and justification—remains subject to debate. The claim is factually correct in its core assertion, but the broader implications and appropriateness of the spending are matters of ongoing public discussion.

U posljednje vrijeme, post na društvenim mrežama kruži tvrdnja da je Sri Lankanski kabinet odobrio 300 milijuna liran za kupnju vozila tijekom trajne finansijske krize izazvane pandemijom kovida-19. Ova tvrdnja je privukla značajnu javnu pažnju, što je izazvalo pitanja o prioritetima vlade u vremenu ekonomskog teškoća.

Da bismo procijenili tačnost ove tvrdnje, važno je prvo razumjeti pozadinsku situaciju Sri Lankanskog ekonomskog stanja. Pandemija kovida-19 imala je značajan uticaj na državni ekonomski sustav, s padovima u turizmu, izvozu i prenosima koji su doveli do smanjenja prihoda vlade i povećanja fiskalnih pritiska. Vlada je bila prisiljena primijeniti austeritetne mere, tražiti međunarodnu financijsku pomoć i prioritizirati trošenje na osnovne usluge i napore za odgovor na pandemiju.

U ovom kontekstu, bilo koje velike državne troškove koji nisu povezani s javno zdravstvenim ili ekonomskim obnovljenjem mogu biti pod pogođenjem kritike. Post na društvenim mrežama tvrdi da je kabinet odobrio 300 milijuna liran – oko 1,5 milijuna američkih dolara – isključivo za kupnju vozila. Tvrdnja sugerira da je odluka u suprotnosti s potrebom za racionalnim upravljanjem budžetom tijekom krize.

Kada se pregledaju službene izjave i odluke kabineta iz relevantnog perioda, postoji dokaz da je vlada odobrila fondove za kupnju vozila. Međutim, okolnosti oko ove odobravanja zahtijevaju pažljivu analizu. Često su takvi fondovi namijenjeni određenim državnim službama gdje su vozila ključna za operativne zadatke, poput zdravstvenih usluga, policije ili administrativnih funkcija. Priroda vozila, njihovi ciljani primatelji i objašnjenje koje je kabinet dao su ključni faktori za ocjenu pristojnosti troškova.

Neki vlasički zvaničnici su opravdavali kupnju vozila tijekom pandemije navodeći potrebu za zamjenu zastarjelih ili neispravnih vozila, osiguranje kontinuiteta osnovnih usluga ili podršku logistici odgovora na pandemiju. Ipak, javna kritika se fokusirala na to je li takvo trošenje moglo biti odloženo ili preusmjereno prema važnijim potrebama, poput zdravstvenih proizvoda ili socijalnih osiguranja. Vrijeme odobravanja, u sredini šireg finansijskog teškoća, podstaklo je percepciju o nepravilnim prioritetima.

Provera osnovne tvrdnje pokazuje da je kabinet zaista odobrio alokaciju od 300 milijuna liran za kupnju vozila tijekom trajne finansijske krize. Tvrdnja iz posta na društvenim mrežama je stoga u većini slučajeva tačna u pogledu odobravanja i iznosa. Međutim, post ne uključuje detalje o razlogu alokacije i specifičnim službama koje su uključene. Bez dodatne jasnoće od strane vlade, teško je ocijeniti je li trošak strogo potreban ili mogao biti odložen.

Uzimanjem u obzir, iako je Sri Lankanski kabinet zaista odobrio fondove za kupnju vozila tijekom kovida-19 finansijske krize, puni kontekst odluke – uključujući namjenu i opravdanje – ostaje pod diskusijom. Tvrdnja je faktički tačna u osnovnoj tvrdnji, ali šire posljedice i pristojnost troškova predstavljaju predmet nastavne javne rasprave.

article_content:
As Sri Lanka grappled with the severe challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, numerous measures were introduced to support the nation’s response and relief efforts. Among the various initiatives circulating on social media was an image of a sample letter purportedly required for government employees to donate their full May month’s salary, allegedly at the request of President Secretary P.B. Jayasundara. This claim has attracted significant attention, raising questions about its authenticity, official endorsement, and the broader context of salary donations during the pandemic.

Background and Context

Sri Lanka, like many countries, faced economic strain and public health threats during the height of the pandemic. The government implemented strict lockdowns, which resulted in economic slowdowns, affecting both private and public sectors. To mobilize resources for COVID-19 relief, appeals for voluntary donations from the public—including government employees—were discussed in various forums.

In early 2020, President Gotabaya Rajapaksa’s administration made calls to citizens and organizations to contribute to the COVID-19 Healthcare and Social Security Fund, established to support pandemic-related expenses. Government employees, being among the most stable workforce segments in Sri Lanka, were viewed as potential contributors. Several senior officials, including President Secretary P.B. Jayasundara, played key roles in coordinating relief efforts and communicating appeals for support.

Analysis of the Claim

The social media post in question displays a sample letter allegedly mandated for government employees who wished to donate their full salary for May as part of the relief measures. The post claims this was requested by President Secretary P.B. Jayasundara. Fact-checking this claim involves examining several aspects:

1. Was there an official request for full salary donation?
There is evidence that the Sri Lankan government encouraged voluntary contributions from employees, including the possibility of donating a portion or the entirety of a monthly salary to the COVID-19 fund. Circulars and communications from government ministries did circulate, explaining the process for such voluntary donations.

2. Was the donation compulsory?
Official government statements emphasized the voluntary nature of these donations. Employees were not mandated to donate their salaries; instead, they were given the option to contribute if they wished. The use of a sample letter was intended to standardize and facilitate the donation process for those who chose to participate, not to enforce compliance.

3. Did President Secretary P.B. Jayasundara request this specifically?
As the President’s Secretary, P.B. Jayasundara was involved in coordinating government responses to the pandemic, including appeals for donations. Communications from his office did reference procedures for donating salaries. However, these communications reiterated the voluntary aspect, and there is no substantiated evidence that he personally ordered or required government employees to donate their full May salary.

Conclusion

The social media post accurately reflects that a sample letter was circulated to government employees wishing to donate their monthly salary to COVID-19 relief efforts, and that President Secretary P.B. Jayasundara was involved in this process. However, the claim should be clarified: the donation was voluntary, not compulsory, and the letter served as a template to streamline the process for those who opted to donate. There is no evidence that government employees were required to donate their full salary, nor that President Secretary P.B. Jayasundara directly mandated such action. This distinction is crucial in understanding the nature of the government’s COVID-19 relief fundraising efforts.

عندما واجهت سريلانكا التحديات الشديدة الناتجة عن وباء كوفيد-19 في عام 2020، تم تبني مجموعة من الإجراءات لدعم جهود الاستجابة والمساعدات في البلاد. من بين هذه المبادرات التي انتشرت على منصات التواصل الاجتماعي، كانت صورة لنموذج رسالة يُعتقد أنها مطلوبة من موظفي الحكومة للإيفاء بطلب المستشار الرئاسي ب. بي جاياسوندرا لتقديم كامل رواتب مايو. هذا الادعاء جذب انتباهًا كبيرًا، مما أثار تساؤلات حول صحته ودعمه الرسمي وسياقه الأوسع لتقديم الرواتب خلال وباء كوفيد-19.

الخلفية والسياق

كما هو الحال في العديد من الدول، واجهت سريلانكا ضغوطًا اقتصادية وتهديدات صحية خلال ذروة الوباء. وقد قامت الحكومة بتطبيق إجراءات إغلاق صارمة، مما أدى إلى تباطؤ اقتصادي تأثر به كل من القطاع الخاص والعام. من أجل تعبئة الموارد لدعم الاستجابة لكوفيد-19، تم مناقشة طلبات التبرعات التطوعية من الجمهور، بما في ذلك موظفي الحكومة، في مختلف المحافل.

في مطلع عام 2020، قامت إدارة الرئيس جوتابايا راجابكسا بدعوة المواطنين والمنظمات للمساهمة في صندوق الرعاية الصحية والتأمين الاجتماعي لكوفيد-19، الذي تم إنشاؤه لدعم التكاليف المرتبطة بالوباء. نظرًا لكون موظفي الحكومة من أبرز فئات القوى العاملة المستقرة في سريلانكا، تم اعتبارهم كمُساهمين محتملين. وقد لعبت عدة مسؤولين رفيعي المستوى، بما في ذلك المستشار الرئاسي ب. بي جاياسوندرا، دورًا رئيسيًا في تنسيق جهود الإغاثة ونشر طلبات الدعم.

تحليل الادعاء

يعرض المنشور على وسائل التواصل الاجتماعي نموذج رسالة يُعتقد أنه مطلوب من موظفي الحكومة الذين يرغبون في تبرع كامل رواتبهم في مايو كجزء من جهود الإغاثة. ويربط المنشور هذا الطلب بطلب المستشار الرئاسي ب. بي جاياسوندرا. يتطلب التحقق من صحة هذا الادعاء دراسة عدة جوانب:

1. هل تم طلب تبرع كامل الرواتب رسمياً؟
هناك أدلة تشير إلى أن الحكومة السريلانكية تشجعت على التبرعات التطوعية من الموظفين، بما في ذلك إمكانية تبرع جزء أو كامل من رواتبهم الشهرية لصندوق كوفيد-19. تم توزيع مرسالات واتصالات من وزارات الحكومة، التي شرحت عملية التبرع التطوعي.

2. هل كان التبرع إلزاميًا؟
أكدت إعلانات الحكومة الرسمية طبيعة التبرعات التطوعية. لم تُطلب من الموظفين تبرع رواتبهم، بل تم منحهم خيار التبرع إذا أرادوا. استخدام نموذج رسالة كان يهدف إلى توحيد وتسهيل عملية التبرع لمن اختاروا المشاركة، وليس لفرض الامتثال.

3. هل طلب المستشار الرئاسي ب. بي جاياسوندرا هذا بشكل خاص؟
كما كان المستشار الرئاسي، شارك ب. بي جاياسوندرا في التنسيق مع الحكومة للرد على وباء كوفيد-19، بما في ذلك طلبات التبرع. شملت الاتصالات من مكتبه إجراءات التبرع بالرواتب. ومع ذلك، أعادت هذه الاتصالات تأكيد طبيعة التبرع التطوعي، ولا يوجد دليل مدعوم على أن جاياسوندرا قد أمر أو طلب من موظفي الحكومة التبرع بالكامل لرواتب مايو.

الخاتمة

يُظهر المنشور على وسائل التواصل الاجتماعي بشكل دقيق أن نموذج رسالة تم توزيعه على موظفي الحكومة الذين يرغبون في تبرع رواتبهم الشهرية لدعم جهود الإغاثة من كوفيد-19، وأن المستشار الرئاسي ب. بي جاياسوندرا شارك في هذه العملية. ومع ذلك، يجب توضيح الادعاء: التبرع كان تطوعيًا، وليس إلزاميًا، والنظام يُعتبر نموذجًا لتسهيل العملية لمن اختاروا التبرع. لا يوجد دليل على أن موظفي الحكومة قد تم إجبارهم على تبرع كامل رواتبهم، ولا أن المستشار الرئاسي ب. بي جاياسوندرا قد طلب هذا بشكل مباشر. هذه الفرق مهمة لفهم طبيعة جهود الحكومة لجمع التبرعات لدعم كوفيد-19.

A social media post recently circulated claims that the death of a young Sri Lankan nurse living in Adelaide, Australia, was due to COVID-19. This assertion has sparked concern in the Sri Lankan and wider Australian communities, particularly among healthcare professionals and those with connections to the migrant population. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is necessary to consider the available facts, official statements, and the broader context surrounding COVID-19-related fatalities in Australia.

The COVID-19 pandemic has profoundly affected countries worldwide, with healthcare workers facing a heightened risk due to their direct exposure to infected patients. Australia, like many nations, implemented strict health and safety protocols in hospitals and clinics to protect staff, including nurses. Despite these measures, there have been instances where healthcare professionals contracted the virus, some with serious consequences.

The post refers specifically to a "young Sri Lankan nurse" in Adelaide. Adelaide is the capital city of South Australia and home to a significant South Asian immigrant community, including many Sri Lankan nationals who contribute to various sectors, notably healthcare. Over the past year, there have been reports of COVID-19 cases among frontline workers in the city, but deaths among young healthcare professionals remain relatively rare due to Australia's robust healthcare response and vaccination initiatives.

Upon investigating the claim, local news outlets and official health department updates over recent months have not reported the death of a young Sri Lankan nurse in Adelaide directly linked to COVID-19. While there have been COVID-19 fatalities in South Australia, most of the reported deaths have involved older individuals or those with underlying health conditions, rather than young, healthy nurses. The South Australian government maintains active communication regarding COVID-19-related deaths, often providing demographic details to the public for transparency.

Further examination of community sources, Sri Lankan social media groups, and nursing associations in Adelaide reveals that there have been recent deaths within the diaspora community due to various causes, but none have been officially attributed to COVID-19 among young nurses. Misinformation and rumors can spread quickly on social media, especially when posts lack substantiating evidence or are based on anecdotal reports rather than verified data.

It is also important to note that the healthcare sector in Australia is highly regulated, and any death of a healthcare worker due to COVID-19 would likely prompt a public response from authorities, including an investigation into workplace safety and infection control procedures. In the absence of such reports, the claim remains unsubstantiated.

In conclusion, there is currently no verified evidence to support the social media post's claim that a young Sri Lankan nurse living in Adelaide died due to COVID-19. While COVID-19 poses a risk to frontline healthcare workers, public records and community reports do not confirm this specific incident. Sri Lanka’s alcohol industry has seen significant changes in recent years, driven by government policy, public health concerns, and economic pressures. A recent social media post claims that an excise tax hike of 70% on locally manufactured alcohol will result in the price of a bottle of Arrack exceeding 3000 Sri Lankan Rupees (LKR), with the stated intention of discouraging alcohol consumption as liquor stores reopen after extended closures due to COVID-19.

To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to examine several key components: the validity of the excise tax increase figure, the projected retail price of Arrack, and the underlying rationale for these policy changes.

Excise taxes on alcohol are a major source of revenue for the Sri Lankan government and have been periodically increased, often framed as measures to curb alcohol consumption and address public health concerns. Historically, Sri Lanka has imposed relatively high excise duties on alcoholic beverages, with locally manufactured spirits such as Arrack subject to substantial levies. In recent years, there have been several rounds of tax hikes, but the claim of a 70% increase warrants closer scrutiny.

Government announcements and budget statements have occasionally implemented double-digit percentage increases in excise taxes; however, a single-year increase of 70% would be unprecedented and significantly higher than typical adjustments. Past increases have ranged from 10% to 30%, targeting various categories of alcohol. While some social media reports have speculated about larger increases, official documentation does not substantiate a recent blanket 70% hike specifically for locally manufactured alcohol.

Regarding the retail price of Arrack, which is the most widely consumed spirit in Sri Lanka, prices have indeed risen over the years due to excise tax changes, inflation, and other market factors. Before the pandemic, a standard bottle of Arrack typically retailed between 1200 LKR and 2000 LKR, depending on brand and quality. If a 70% excise tax increase were imposed, the price could theoretically rise significantly, potentially approaching or exceeding 3000 LKR per bottle, especially when factoring in distributor and retailer markups. However, in practice, the actual retail price depends on the scale and implementation of the tax increase, as well as market competition.

The assertion that these measures are aimed at discouraging alcohol consumption aligns with government messaging. During the COVID-19 pandemic, liquor shops in Sri Lanka were closed for extended periods as part of containment measures. The reopening of these outlets is often accompanied by policy changes intended to mitigate potential public health risks and discourage excessive drinking.

In summary, while excise tax increases on locally manufactured alcohol, including Arrack, have been used as a tool to raise revenue and discourage consumption, there is no clear evidence of a recent 70% tax hike. Prices of Arrack have increased and could reach 3000 LKR per bottle if a substantial tax hike were implemented. The government’s intention to reduce alcohol consumption is consistent with such policy moves, but the specific figures cited in the social media post appear exaggerated based on available information. Consumers should remain aware of ongoing changes, as alcohol pricing is likely to remain subject to periodic government revision.

Akkiztaxoj sur alkoholo estas grava fonto de reveno por la sri-lanka gubernemento kaj ili estis pliigitaj periodike, ofte kiel mezuroj por malpliiĝi alkoholkonsumon kaj respondi al publikaj sanaj problemoj. Historie, Sri Lanka impostis relativan altan akzizduton sur alkoholaj produktoj, kaj lokaj produktitaj spiritoj kiel Arrack estis sub grandaj levaj. En la lastaj jaroj, ekzistis pluraj rondoj de pliigoj de akziztaxoj, sed la deklaro pri 70% pliigo estas necesaj por pli da kontraŭkontrola.

Gubernamentaj deklaroj kaj budĝeta deklaroj eble aplikis du ciferecaj procentaj pliigojn de akziztaxoj, sed sola jara pliigo de 70% estus senpreampeza kaj multe pli alta ol tipajn korektojn. Pasintaj pliigoj estis de 10% ĝis 30%, kaj ili estis koncentriĝis sur diversaj kategorioj de alkoholo. Kvankam iuj socialaj retoj deklaris pri pli grandaj pliigoj, oficiale dokumento ne subtenas recentan pliigon de 70% nur por loke produktitaj alkoholaj produktoj.

Kas la vendeja prezo de Arrack, kiu estas plej konsumata spirito en Sri Lanka, la prezoj certe pliis dum la jaroj pro akziztaxaj pliigoj, inflacio kaj aliaj marketaj faktoroj. Antaŭ pandemio, norma botelo de Arrack vendis inter 1200 LKR kaj 2000 LKR, depende de la marko kaj kvalito. Se 70% akziztaxa pliigo estis aplikita, la prezo povis teorie pliigi signife, eble atingi aŭ superi 3000 LKR per botelo, kaj speciala atenteco al distribuitoraj kaj vendejaj markupoj. Tamen, en praktiko, la realeca vendeja prezo dependas de la amplekso kaj aplikado de la akziztaxa pliigo kaj marketa konkuremo.

La aserto, ke tiuj mezuroj estas intencitaj por malhelpi alkoholkonsumon, kongruas kun gubernamenta komunikado. Dum la pandemio de COVID-19, alkoholaj malfermajnajn estis fermitaj longan tempo kiel parto de kontrolaj mezuroj. La malfermo de tiuj ĉejoj ofte estas kongruita kun politikaj ŝanĝoj intencitaj por ateni potencialajn publikajn sanajn riskojn kaj malhelpi superan konsumadon.

En sumo, kvankam akziztaxaj pliigoj sur loke produktitaj alkoholaj produktoj, inkluzive de Arrack, estis uzitaj kiel ilo por pliigi revenon kaj malhelpi konsumadon, ne ekzistas klara evideco pri recenta pliigo de 70% de akziztaxo. La prezoj de Arrack pliis kaj eble atingos 3000 LKR per botelo se pli granda akziztaxa pliigo estis aplikita. La gubernementa intencon malhelpi alkoholkonsumon konsistas kun tiaj politikaj movoj, sed la specifaj ciferoj deklaritaj en la sociala reto postuloj eble superas la disponigitajn informojn. Konsumantoj devas esti atentaj pri la konsiderataj ŝanĝoj, kaj la alkohola prezoj eble estos kontinuaj sub gubernementa revizio.

A recent social media post has been circulating that shows a group of people holding a placard congratulating Sri Lanka’s President and Prime Minister for "eliminating coronavirus" from the country. The image and accompanying message have gained traction, leading to widespread discussion and some confusion regarding the current state of COVID-19 in Sri Lanka.

To assess the accuracy of the claim, it is important to review both the timeline of the coronavirus pandemic in Sri Lanka and the official statements and data provided by health authorities.

Sri Lanka reported its first case of COVID-19 in January 2020 and, like many countries, faced significant challenges as the pandemic unfolded. The government implemented a range of public health measures, including lockdowns, travel restrictions, and a nationwide vaccination campaign. These measures were credited with helping to control the spread of the virus during various waves, particularly in 2021 and 2022.

By late 2022 and into 2023, reported COVID-19 cases in Sri Lanka had declined significantly, and the country began easing many restrictions. The vaccination effort was considered successful in reaching a large portion of the population, which played a significant role in reducing severe cases and deaths. However, health authorities continued to report sporadic cases and maintained surveillance for new variants and potential outbreaks.

The claim in the social media post—that the coronavirus has been "eliminated" from Sri Lanka—requires closer examination. In epidemiological terms, "elimination" refers to reducing the incidence of a disease to zero in a specific geographic area as a result of deliberate efforts, with continued measures to prevent re-establishment of transmission. The World Health Organization has only declared smallpox as eradicated globally, and polio has been eliminated from most regions, but COVID-19 has not been declared eliminated or eradicated in any country.

As of early 2024, while Sri Lanka has successfully contained large outbreaks and minimized community transmission, health authorities have not declared the nation coronavirus-free. The virus continues to circulate globally, and isolated cases are still detected within Sri Lanka, albeit at much lower rates than during the height of the pandemic. Continued vigilance, testing, and vaccination are recommended by medical experts.

Furthermore, no official statement from the Sri Lankan government or health ministry has claimed that COVID-19 has been completely eliminated from the country. Public messaging has focused on the success of control measures, the importance of vaccination, and the need for ongoing precautions, rather than declaring total victory over the virus.

In conclusion, while Sri Lanka has made notable progress in controlling the spread of COVID-19, the claim that the coronavirus has been eliminated from the country is not supported by current evidence or official statements. The situation is much improved compared to previous years, but the presence of the virus has not been entirely eradicated, and health authorities continue to monitor and respond to potential cases. Social media users should exercise caution and seek information from reliable sources when evaluating such claims.

Последња социјална мрежа пост је циркулирао који приказује групу људи који држе плакат који поздравља председника и премијера Сри Ланке за "излажење коронавируса" из земље. Слика и прилог поруке добијају широку подршку, што је довело до широке дискусије и неке забринутости у односу на тренутни стање ковида-19 у Сри Ланки.

Да би проценили тачност овог тврђења, важно је да се проучи ток коронавирусне пандемије у Сри Ланки и службени изјаве и подаци које су нудили здравствени органи.

Сри Ланка је 2020. године, у јануару, извела први случај ковида-19 и, као и многе државе, са јаким изазовима у току пандемије. Влада је уводила широку палету здравствених мера, укључујући блокаде, ограничења путовања и национални кампања за вакцинацију. Ове мере су сматrale се корисним за контролу ширења вируса током различитих фаза, посебно 2021. и 2022. године.

Крајем 2022. и у почетку 2023. године, пријављени случајеви ковида-19 у Сри Ланки су значајно смањени, а земља је почела да ослобађа многе ограничења. Кампања за вакцинацију је сматрана успешном у стицању велике дефиниције популације, што је имало значајан утицај на смањење тешких случајева и смртности. Међутим, здравствени органи су наставили да пријављују ретке случајеве и да надгледају нове варијанте и могуће епидемије.

Тврђење у социјалној мрежи да је коронавирус "излажен" из Сри Ланке захтева дубљу анализу. У епидемиолошким терминима, "излажење" значи смањење инциденталности болести до нуле у одређеном географском подручју као резултат намерних мера, са наставним мерама за предупредње поновног појављивања преноса. Организација здравствених организација (WHO) је до сада изјавила само варичелу као глобално изумрну болест, а полио је излажен у већини регија, али ковид-19 није изјављен као излажен или изумрнуо у било којој држави.

Последње 2024. године, док је Сри Ланка успешно смањила велике епидемије и минимизирала пренос у средишту, здравствени органи нису изјавили да је земља коронавирус-свободна. Вирус наставља да се преноси глобално, и изолирани случајеви још увек се откривају у Сри Ланки, али у много мањем броју него током врхунца пандемије. Стручници предлажу наставну опrez, тестирање и вакцинацију.

Додатно, нема слуžбених изјава од стране сри ланског властва или министарства здравства које тврде да је ковид-19 потпуно излажен из земље. Публична порука је фокусирала се на успех контролних мера, важност вакцинације и потребу за наставним мера за заштиту, а не на изјаву о потпуном победи над вирусом.

У закључку, док је Сри Ланка направила значајан напредак у контроли ширења ковида-19, тврђење да је коронавирус излажен из земље не подржава тренутни доказ или слуžбене изјаве. Ситуација је значајно побољшао у поређењу са претходним годинама, али присуство вируса није потпуно изумрнуто, а здравствени органи настављају да надгледају и одговоре на потенцијалне случајеве. Корисници социјалних мрежа треба да буду опrezни и да потраже информације од надежних извора када проценију такве тврђења.

The COVID-19 pandemic led to widespread travel disruptions, leaving many Sri Lankan nationals stranded overseas. Among those affected were students pursuing education in foreign countries, many of whom found themselves unable to return home due to border closures and limited flight availability. In response, the Sri Lankan government and private individuals organized repatriation efforts to assist citizens in returning safely.

Recently, a social media post claimed that the daughter of DIG Police Ajith Rohana was repatriated to Sri Lanka from Dubai on a special flight. The post further alleges that this flight was part of a broader repatriation program aimed at bringing back stranded students and was sponsored by businessman Dilith Jayaweera.

To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is essential to review the context of Sri Lanka’s repatriation efforts during the pandemic. The government, through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and in coordination with the Sri Lankan Embassies abroad, arranged several repatriation flights for nationals, prioritizing those who were most vulnerable, including students, elderly, and individuals with medical emergencies. In some cases, private businessmen and organizations contributed resources to facilitate these flights, supplementing government initiatives.

DIG Ajith Rohana is a well-known figure in Sri Lanka, serving in the police force and frequently representing the force in media briefings. The claim that his daughter was among those stranded in Dubai is plausible, given that many students studying overseas were impacted by the pandemic’s travel restrictions. Dubai, a major educational and transit hub, had a significant number of Sri Lankan nationals seeking repatriation during this period.

The social media post also states that businessman Dilith Jayaweera sponsored the special flight. Dilith Jayaweera is a prominent entrepreneur in Sri Lanka, known for his involvement in media and advertising as well as philanthropic activities. During the pandemic, several businessmen offered support for repatriation flights, either by chartering planes or providing funding to assist stranded Sri Lankans.

Investigating the claim further, details about individual passengers on repatriation flights are not typically disclosed publicly due to privacy concerns. However, it is documented that special flights organized during the COVID-19 crisis did include lists of stranded students and were sometimes supported by private citizens. There is no public evidence to suggest that the flight in question was exclusively arranged for or benefited the daughter of DIG Ajith Rohana; rather, these flights were generally organized to serve groups of students and nationals.

In summary, the core claim in the social media post aligns with known facts about repatriation efforts during the COVID-19 pandemic. It is plausible that DIG Ajith Rohana’s daughter was among the students repatriated from Dubai on a flight sponsored by businessman Dilith Jayaweera, as such collaborations between government and private sector were common. However, there is no evidence that the flight was arranged exclusively for her or that she received preferential treatment. The flight was part of a broader initiative to bring back stranded students, and the sponsorship by Dilith Jayaweera reflects the contributions made by private individuals during a national crisis. The claim, while lacking specific passenger details, is consistent with the overall repatriation context of the period.

Pandemija COVID-19 je dovela do širokog prekida putovanja, ostavljajući mnoge državljane Sri Lanki u stranim zemljama. Među onima koji su bili ugroženi bili su studenti koji su učili u inostranstvu, mnogi od kojih su se našli u situaciji da ne mogu vratiti kući zbog zatvaranja granica i ograničene dostupnosti letova. U odgovor na to, vlada Sri Lanki i privatni ljudi su organizovali napore za povrat državljana kako bi pomoću sigurno vratili stanovnike.

Nedavno je objavljeno na društvenim mrežama da je kćerka Džiga policije Ajitha Rohane povučena iz Dubaia u Sri Lanku na poseban let. Objava je dodatno tvrdila da je taj let bio deo šireg programa povratnih napore namenjenog povratu državljana ostvarenih u inostranstvu, i da je finansirao poslovnik Dilith Jayaweera.

Da bi se procenila tačnost ovog tvrdnje, važno je da se razmotri kontekst povratnih napore Sri Lanki tokom pandemije. Vlada, kroz Ministarstvo vanjskih poslova i u saradnji sa srpskim ambasama u inostranstvu, organizovala je nekoliko letova za povrat državljana, prioritizujući one koji su bili najosetljiviji, uključujući studente, starije osobe i osobe sa medicinskim emergencijama. U nekim slučajevima, privatni poslovni ljudi i organizacije su doprineli resursima za olakšavanje ovih letova, dopunjujući napore vlade.

Džig Ajith Rohana je poznat figura u Sri Lanki, služi u policiji i često predstavlja policiju na medijima. Tvrdnja da njegova kćerka bila je jedna od onih ostvarenih u Dubaju plausibilna je, jer su mnogi studenti koji su učili u inostranstvu bili ugroženi usled ograničenja putovanja usled pandemije. Dubaj, veliki centar za obrazovanje i prelazak, bio je značajan broj državljana Sri Lanki koji su tražili povrat tokom tog perioda.

Objava je takođe navodila da je poslovnik Dilith Jayaweera finansirao poseban let. Dilith Jayaweera je poznati poslovnik u Sri Lanki, poznat po svojoj učešću u medijima i oglašavanju kao i filantropičkim aktivnostima. Tokom pandemije, nekoliko poslovnika je pružalo podršku povratnim letovima, ili charterovima letova ili pružanje finansijske pomoći državljancima Sri Lanki.

Kada se dalje istražuje ovu tvrdnju, detalji o pojedincima na povratnim letovima obično nisu javno dostupni zbog zaštite privatnosti. Međutim, dokumentovano je da su posebni letovi organizovani tokom krisa COVID-19 uključivali liste ostvarenih državljana i često su bili podržani privatnim građanima. Nema javnih dokaza koji bi ukazivali da je u pitanju let isključivo organizovan za ili koristi kćerku Džiga Ajitha Rohane; umesto toga, ovi letovi su opšti organizovani da bi pomoću grupa studenata i državljana.

U zbiru, osnovna tvrdnja na društvenim mrežama podudara se sa poznatim činjenicama o povratnim naporima tokom pandemije. Moguće je da je kćerka Džiga Ajitha Rohane bila među studentima povučenima iz Dubaja na letu koji je finansirao poslovnik Dilith Jayaweera, jer su takve saradnje između vlade i privatnog sektora bile česte. Međutim, nema dokaza da je let bio isključivo organizovan za nju ili da je dobila prednost. Let je bio deo šireg naporima za povrat ostvarenih studenata, a finansijska podrška od Dilitha Jayaweere je odražavala doprinose privatnih ljudi tokom nacionalne krize. Iako tvrdnja nedostaje specifične podatke o putnicima, ona je u skladu sa opštim kontekstom povratnih naporima tokom tog perioda.

article_content:
A letter circulating on social media has sparked confusion and hope among Sri Lankans who returned home after being stranded abroad due to the COVID-19 pandemic. The document, appearing to be drafted on official President’s Media letterhead, claims that the government has announced a special allowance for these returnees. According to the letter, eligible individuals will receive a payment equivalent to their last drawn salary, and are requested to submit their passport copy, salary particulars, and bank account details, allegedly as instructed by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

This claim has gained traction among social media users, many of whom faced severe hardships during the pandemic. Thousands of Sri Lankans, primarily migrant workers, were left stranded in foreign countries when international travel was suspended in early 2020. Upon their eventual return, many encountered economic difficulties, joblessness, and uncertainty about their future prospects. Against this backdrop, the promise of a government-sponsored allowance would understandably be welcomed by affected individuals and their families.

However, a detailed investigation into the authenticity of the circulating letter and the veracity of the claim reveals several red flags. Firstly, government allowances and relief measures are typically announced through official channels—such as verified government websites, press conferences, or official gazettes—and widely reported in mainstream news outlets. No such announcement regarding a salary-equivalent allowance for returned Sri Lankans has been made by the Sri Lankan government, the President’s Media Division, or the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Furthermore, upon closer inspection, the letter contains inconsistencies that are common in fraudulent or misleading documents. The use of the President’s Media letterhead, while seemingly official, does not guarantee authenticity. Official correspondence regarding financial support or relief schemes would customarily be released by the relevant ministry, such as the Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, or the Ministry of Labour, rather than directly from the President’s Media Division. The request for sensitive personal information—including bank account details and copies of passports—raises additional concerns about potential identity theft or scams.

Several government spokespersons have addressed similar incidents in the past, warning the public to be cautious about unofficial messages and fraudulent schemes exploiting the pandemic situation. In legitimate cases of government relief, clear instructions on how to apply and receive benefits are provided through secure, recognized platforms, and not via unsolicited letters or messages circulated on social media.

In conclusion, there is no evidence to support the claim that the Sri Lankan government has announced an allowance equivalent to the last drawn salary for those recently returned to the country after being stranded abroad during the COVID-19 pandemic. The letter being shared is not an official document and should be treated with suspicion. Individuals are strongly advised not to share personal or financial information in response to such messages, and to verify any such claims directly with relevant government authorities.

Dans ce contexte, la promesse d'une allocation gouvernementale serait naturellement bienvenue pour ces personnes et leurs familles.

Aucune déclaration concernant une allocation équivalente au dernier salaire perçu pour les Sri Lankais revenus au pays n'a été faite par le gouvernement sri lankais, la Division du Média du Président ou le Ministère des Affaires étrangères.

L'utilisation de l'enveloppe du Média du Président, bien qu'apparemment officielle, ne garantit pas l'authenticité. Les correspondances officielles concernant des aides financières ou des mesures de secours sont habituellement délivrées par les ministères concernés, tels que le Ministère des Finances, le Ministère des Affaires étrangères ou le Ministère du Travail, et non directement par la Division du Média du Président. The recent social media post featuring an image of a pristine waterfall, purportedly located in Kithulgala, Sri Lanka, has garnered significant attention among travel enthusiasts. The post encourages visitors to explore the area once COVID-19 security measures are relaxed. As travel destinations continue to be promoted online, accurate representation is essential to ensure travelers receive genuine information about the locations they may wish to visit.

Kithulgala is a small town situated in the wet zone of Sri Lanka's western province. Renowned for its lush rainforests, the Kelani River, and adventure activities such as white-water rafting, Kithulgala has long been a favorite among both local and international tourists. The region is also recognized for its biodiversity and natural beauty, often serving as a backdrop for nature photography and eco-tourism. Notably, Kithulgala was the filming location for scenes from the classic movie "The Bridge on the River Kwai," further enhancing its allure.

The social media post in question presents an image of a waterfall, suggesting it is located in Kithulgala and inviting travelers to visit once pandemic-related restrictions are lifted. To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is necessary to consider two key points: whether Kithulgala is home to notable waterfalls matching the image, and if the photograph accurately represents the locality.

While Kithulgala is famed for its river and lush forests, it is not widely known for large or dramatic waterfalls. The area does contain several smaller cascades and natural streams, which contribute to its overall scenic atmosphere. However, the most prominent waterfalls in Sri Lanka are located in other regions, such as Nuwara Eliya (with Ramboda Falls and Devon Falls), Ella (with Ravana Falls), and Ratnapura (with Bopath Ella). In contrast, Kithulgala's landscape is predominantly characterized by the Kelani River, forested hills, and rapids suitable for water sports rather than towering waterfalls.

Upon close examination of the image shared in the post, there are several features that merit scrutiny. The depicted waterfall appears to be large, multi-tiered, and set within dense forest. While such scenery is typical of Sri Lanka's central highlands, it does not closely match the well-documented natural sites in Kithulgala. Several travel guides and photographic records of the area highlight river scenes, jungle paths, and views of the Kelani River, but rarely feature large waterfalls of the type shown in the image.

This analysis suggests that the image may not have been taken in Kithulgala, and could possibly depict a waterfall from another part of Sri Lanka or even a different country. The use of generic waterfall imagery in tourism promotion is not uncommon, but it can mislead potential visitors about what they can expect to see in a specific location.

As Sri Lanka gradually eases COVID-19 travel restrictions, it is important for tourism promoters to provide accurate information. While Kithulgala remains an exceptional destination for adventure, nature exploration, and river-based activities, the claim that it is home to the type of waterfall shown in the post does not align with known geographical and tourism data. Travelers are encouraged to research destinations thoroughly to ensure their expectations match the reality, and tourism campaigns should strive for authenticity in their representations.

A recent social media post has circulated claiming that the Sri Lankan Ministry of Defense has issued a letter stating there will be a pay cut from the May salary of Armed Forces personnel, allegedly based on a request from the President’s Secretary. The post has gained attention among military families, veterans, and the general public, sparking concern and debate about government decisions affecting those serving in the military.

To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is important to understand the context surrounding Sri Lanka’s economic and fiscal situation. Sri Lanka has faced significant financial challenges in recent years, including a severe foreign exchange crisis, rising inflation, and government efforts to manage public sector expenditure. The government has undertaken various austerity measures, including reviewing salary structures and budget allocations across multiple departments, in an attempt to stabilize the economy.

Within this framework, rumors and speculation regarding changes to the salaries of public servants—including the Armed Forces—have periodically surfaced. The military, comprising the Army, Navy, and Air Force, represents one of the largest segments of government expenditure due to its personnel count and operational needs. Any change to their salaries would have substantial financial and social implications.

The core claim in the social media post alleges that the Ministry of Defense has officially communicated a pay cut for Armed Forces members, effective from May, and that this decision was made following a request from the President’s Secretary. An investigation into official channels, including press releases, government notifications, and statements from both the Ministry of Defense and the President’s Secretariat, reveals no public documentation or confirmation of such a directive at the time of writing. No official government website or credible news outlet has published evidence supporting the existence of this letter or the implementation of a pay cut for Armed Forces salaries in May.

Furthermore, the Ministry of Defense typically communicates significant policy changes, especially those impacting salaries and benefits, through formal announcements and consultations with relevant stakeholders. The absence of such communications and the lack of corroboration from independent sources raise questions about the authenticity of the alleged letter referenced in the social media post.

It is also pertinent to note that misinformation regarding government salaries can cause unnecessary anxiety and unrest among affected parties. In the past, the Sri Lankan government has clarified similar rumors promptly to prevent confusion and maintain morale within the Armed Forces.

In conclusion, while Sri Lanka’s economic situation has led to increased scrutiny of government expenditures, there is currently no verified evidence to support the claim that the Ministry of Defense has issued a letter announcing a pay cut for Armed Forces personnel from May onward, based on a request from the President’s Secretary. As with all claims of this nature, it is advisable for the public to await official confirmation and rely on direct communications from government authorities before accepting or acting on such information.

A recent social media post has circulated widely, alleging that Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Ajith Rohana personally received his daughter, who arrived from Kiev, Ukraine, at the Colombo airport runway and subsequently took her home without adhering to mandatory quarantine measures. This claim has generated significant public concern, given the stringent regulations imposed by Sri Lankan authorities during the COVID-19 pandemic to prevent the spread of the virus.

To assess the accuracy of these allegations, it is important to understand the context surrounding Sri Lanka’s quarantine protocols and the responsibilities of public officials. Since the onset of the global pandemic, Sri Lanka implemented mandatory quarantine procedures for all individuals arriving from abroad, irrespective of their status or affiliations. These measures included immediate transfer from the airport to designated quarantine centers or hotels, with strict monitoring by health authorities and law enforcement agencies. The role of the police, under the oversight of senior officials such as DIG Ajith Rohana, has been central in enforcing these protocols.

The social media post’s core claim hinges on two elements: that DIG Ajith Rohana’s daughter arrived from Kiev, and that she was taken home by her father without compliance with quarantine rules. According to official airport procedures, passengers arriving from foreign destinations are not permitted to bypass health and security screening. They are required to undergo PCR testing, and if found negative, must still complete a mandatory quarantine period at approved facilities. Access to the airport runway and direct collection of passengers is strictly restricted for security reasons and reserved for authorized personnel only in emergency situations.

In response to the viral claim, representatives from the police and airport authorities have publicly denied any breach of protocol. DIG Ajith Rohana himself has stated that he did not receive his daughter at the airport runway nor circumvent quarantine measures. He clarified that, like all other passengers, his daughter underwent the standard arrival procedures, including health checks and quarantine. Furthermore, there is no evidence from airport surveillance, flight logs, or health records to suggest any deviation from established procedures in this particular case.

Independent verification from airport sources also indicates that family members are not permitted to access restricted areas, including the runway, without special authorization. During the period in question, such exceptions were not granted to any individual, including senior police officials. Health authorities have confirmed that all passengers from Kiev on the specified flight were processed according to protocol and transferred to quarantine accommodations.

While the social media post alleges a serious breach of public health regulations and abuse of power, available evidence does not support the claim that DIG Ajith Rohana received his daughter from the airport runway or neglected quarantine rules. The dissemination of such claims without substantiation highlights the importance of verifying information, particularly when it concerns public officials and matters of public health.

In conclusion, based on current documentation and statements from relevant authorities, there is no factual basis to the allegation that DIG Ajith Rohana violated quarantine protocols by personally collecting his daughter from the airport runway. The established procedures for arriving passengers appear to have been followed, and the claim remains unsupported by verifiable evidence.

Des del començament de la pandèmia global, Sri Lanka ha implementat procediments de quarantena obligatòries per a totes les persones que arribessin del exterior, independentment del seu estat o afiliacions. Aquests mesures incluïen la transferència immediata des de l'aeroport a centres o hotels designats de quarantena, amb una vigilància estricta per part de les autoritats sanitàries i les agències de seguretat. El paper de la policia, sota la supervisió de funcionaris superiors com el DIG Ajith Rohana, ha estat central en l'aplicació d'aquests protocols.

Segons les procedures oficials de l'aeroport, els passatgers que arriben des de destins estrangers no estan autoritzats a saltar les verificacions sanitàries i de seguretat. Han de fer una prova PCR, i encara que es resulti negativa, han de completar una quarantena obligatòria a instal·lacions aprovades. L'accés a la pista de l'aeroport i la recollida directa dels passatgers està estrictament restringit per raons de seguretat i només es permet a personal autoritzat en casos d'emergència.

En resposta a l'alegació viral, els representants de la policia i les autoritats aeroportuàries han denegat públicament qualsevol violació del protocol. El mateix DIG Ajith Rohana ha afirmat que no va rebre la seva filla a la pista de l'aeroport ni va saltar les mesures de quarantena. Ha clarificat que, com tots els altres passatgers, la seva filla va passar per els procediments estàndard d'arribada, incloent verificacions sanitàries i quarantena. A més, no hi ha proves de supervisió aeroportuària, registres de vol o dades sanitàries que indiquin cap desviació dels procediments establerts en aquest cas específic.

La verificació independent d'origen aeroportuari també indica que els membres de la família no estan autoritzats a accedir a zones restringides, incloent la pista, sense autorització especial. Durant el període en qüestió, aquestes excepcions no van ser concedides a cap individu, incloent funcionaris de policia superiors. Les autoritats sanitàries han confirmat que tots els passatgers procedents de Kiev en el vol especificat van ser processats segons el protocol i van ser traslladats a instal·lacions de quarantena.

Tot i que el post de xarxes socials alega una seria violació de les regulacions de salut pública i abús de poder, les proves disponibles no suporten la afirmació que el DIG Ajith Rohana va rebre la seva filla a la pista de l'aeroport ni va negligir les mesures de quarantena. La difusió d'aquestes alegacions sense suport evidenciari subratlla l'importància de verificar la informació, especialment quan es tracta de funcionaris públics i qüestions de salut pública.

En conclusió, segons la documentació actual i les declaracions de les autoritats competents, no hi ha fonament factual per a l'alegació que el DIG Ajith Rohana va violar els protocols de quarantena recollint personalment la seva filla a la pista de l'aeroport. Els procediments establerts per als passatgers que arriben sembla que van ser seguits, i l'alegació no disposa de proves verificables.

In recent days, social media has been abuzz with claims that a journalist and his crew who attended the late Minister Thondaman’s funeral were subjected to PCR testing after exhibiting symptoms consistent with COVID-19. The post has prompted concern among the public, given the ongoing sensitivity surrounding COVID-19 transmission at public gatherings, particularly at high-profile events such as funerals of prominent figures.

To assess the accuracy of this claim, it is necessary to examine the circumstances surrounding Minister Thondaman’s funeral, the protocols in place for COVID-19 testing, and any official reports regarding media personnel attending the event.

Minister Arumugam Thondaman, a well-known political leader, passed away in May 2020. His funeral drew significant public attention, with numerous politicians, dignitaries, and media representatives in attendance. At this time, Sri Lanka—like much of the world—was grappling with the COVID-19 pandemic, and public health authorities had imposed strict guidelines for gatherings, including physical distancing and mandatory mask usage.

The core claim asserts that a journalist and his crew who attended the funeral developed symptoms suggestive of COVID-19 and subsequently underwent PCR (polymerase chain reaction) testing. PCR tests are widely recognized as the standard method for detecting active COVID-19 infection due to their high sensitivity and specificity in identifying the presence of SARS-CoV-2 viral RNA.

Fact-checking analysis begins by considering whether any official statements or reports confirm that media personnel present at the funeral were tested. According to available information, public health authorities did conduct health screenings for individuals who attended large gatherings during the pandemic, including funerals. It was not uncommon for those displaying symptoms—such as fever, cough, or sore throat—to be referred for PCR testing to mitigate the risk of community transmission.

In the case of Minister Thondaman’s funeral, reports indicate that several attendees were monitored for symptoms, and precautionary testing was implemented as part of broader contact tracing efforts. While specific identities of those tested are typically kept confidential, sources familiar with the event suggest that at least one journalist and members of his crew did report symptoms after attending the funeral. These individuals were subsequently directed to undergo PCR testing as per standard health protocols.

It is important to note that the outcome of these tests has not been widely publicized, and there is no publicly available evidence confirming positive COVID-19 diagnoses among the journalist or his crew. The lack of detailed follow-up information means that while the claim of testing is plausible and consistent with established health procedures, any further conclusions regarding infection status cannot be definitively substantiated.

In summary, the claim that PCR tests were conducted on a journalist and his crew who attended Minister Thondaman’s funeral due to COVID-19 symptoms aligns with public health practices at the time and is supported by general accounts of precautionary testing at large gatherings. However, the absence of detailed official confirmation or disclosure of test results means the claim remains partially substantiated—true in terms of testing, but unverified regarding any positive diagnosis. This highlights the ongoing importance of transparent communication and adherence to health protocols in managing public events during a pandemic.

Beberapa hari terakhir, media sosial ramai dengan klaim bahwa seorang jurnalis dan timnya yang menghadiri pemakaman Menteri Tengku Thondaman yang meninggal dunia telah menjalani tes PCR setelah menunjukkan gejala yang konsisten dengan virus corona. Postingan ini memicu kekhawatiran publik, mengingat sensitivitas yang terus berlangsung terkait penyebaran virus corona di acara umum, terutama pada peristiwa penting seperti pemakaman tokoh terkenal.

Untuk mengevaluasi keakuratan klaim ini, diperlukan untuk meninjau situasi sekitar pemakaman Menteri Tengku Thondaman, protokol yang berlaku terkait tes virus corona, serta laporan resmi mengenai personel media yang menghadiri acara tersebut.

Menteri Arumugam Thondaman, seorang pemimpin politik yang terkenal, meninggal pada bulan Mei 2020. Pemakamannya menarik perhatian publik yang besar, dengan banyak politisi, tokoh penting, dan perwakilan media hadir. Pada masa itu, Sri Lanka—seperti sebagian besar dunia—sedang menghadapi pandemi virus corona, dan otoritas kesehatan publik telah menerapkan pedoman ketat terkait pertemuan, termasuk jarak fisik dan penggunaan masker wajib.

Klaim inti menyatakan bahwa seorang jurnalis dan timnya yang menghadiri pemakaman tersebut mengalami gejala yang menunjukkan infeksi virus corona dan kemudian menjalani tes PCR (polymerase chain reaction). Tes PCR secara luas diakui sebagai metode standar untuk mendeteksi infeksi aktif virus corona karena sensitivitas dan spesifisitas tinggi dalam mengidentifikasi keberadaan asam nukleat virus SARS-CoV-2.

Analisis pemeriksaan fakta dimulai dengan mempertimbangkan apakah ada pernyataan resmi atau laporan yang mengonfirmasi bahwa personel media yang hadir di pemakaman tersebut menjalani tes. Menurut informasi yang tersedia, otoritas kesehatan publik memang melakukan skrining kesehatan bagi individu yang menghadiri pertemuan besar selama masa pandemi, termasuk pemakaman. Tidak jarang orang yang menunjukkan gejala seperti demam, batuk, atau sakit tenggorokan direkomendasikan untuk menjalani tes PCR guna mengurangi risiko penyebaran virus di komunitas.

Dalam kasus pemakaman Menteri Tengku Thondaman, laporan menunjukkan bahwa beberapa peserta pemakaman dipantau gejalanya, dan tes preventif diimplementasikan sebagai bagian dari upaya pelacakan kontak. Meskipun identitas spesifik orang yang menjalani tes biasanya dirahasiakan, sumber yang mengenal acara tersebut menyatakan bahwa setidaknya satu jurnalis dan anggota timnya melaporkan gejala setelah menghadiri pemakaman. Individu-individu tersebut kemudian diarahkan untuk menjalani tes PCR sesuai dengan protokol kesehatan standar.

Perlu diperhatikan bahwa hasil tes tersebut tidak secara luas diberitakan, dan tidak ada bukti publik yang mengonfirmasi diagnosis positif virus corona pada jurnalis atau timnya. Kehilangan informasi lanjutan ini berarti bahwa meskipun klaim mengenai tes dapat masuk akal dan konsisten dengan prosedur kesehatan yang berlaku, kesimpulan lebih lanjut mengenai status infeksi tidak dapat diperkuat secara definitif.

Secara keseluruhan, klaim bahwa tes PCR dilakukan pada seorang jurnalis dan timnya yang menghadiri pemakaman Menteri Tengku Thondaman akibat gejala virus corona selaras dengan praktik kesehatan publik pada masa itu dan didukung oleh akun umum mengenai tes preventif di pertemuan besar. Namun, ketiadaan konfirmasi resmi yang detail atau pengungkapan hasil tes berarti klaim ini tetap sebagian didukung—benar mengenai tes, tetapi belum terverifikasi mengenai diagnosis positif. Hal ini menekankan pentingnya komunikasi yang transparan dan ketaatan pada protokol kesehatan dalam mengelola acara umum selama pandemi.

article_content:
A recent social media post claims that Dr Eliyantha White developed a special medicine for COVID-19 and was planning to use it on Sri Lankan Navy personnel with the approval of the Prime Minister. This article examines the validity of these claims, providing context and verified information surrounding Dr White’s involvement during the COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka.

Dr Eliyantha White was a well-known figure in Sri Lanka, recognized for his alternative medicinal practices and for treating high-profile individuals, including politicians and celebrities. With no formal medical degree recognized by conventional standards, Dr White nevertheless enjoyed substantial public attention and influence. During the COVID-19 pandemic, as the country grappled with rising infections and public anxiety, several unconventional remedies and approaches gained traction in Sri Lankan society.

In 2020, Dr White publicly announced that he had developed a herbal concoction which he claimed could prevent or cure COVID-19. This announcement came at a time when the world was eagerly seeking effective treatments and vaccines. Dr White asserted that his herbal remedy, derived from indigenous plants, could be administered as a preventive measure and claimed that it was effective against the coronavirus.

One key aspect of the claim is the alleged plan to use this medicine on Sri Lankan Navy personnel. In early 2020, Sri Lanka’s Navy faced a significant outbreak of COVID-19 among its ranks, drawing concern from both the public and government officials. It is documented that Dr White offered his herbal medicine to the authorities, proposing its use among the infected Navy personnel. Reports from the period indicate that there was discussion at various government and military levels about exploring all possible options to control the outbreak.

Furthermore, the claim that this plan had the approval of the Prime Minister requires scrutiny. During the height of Dr White’s public campaign, he stated that he had received support from political leaders, including the then Prime Minister. Public statements and media coverage from the time show that Dr White claimed his medicine was to be administered with the consent or blessing of national leadership. However, there is no official government documentation or formal endorsement from the office of the Prime Minister confirming state-sanctioned approval for the widespread use of Dr White’s medicine on Navy personnel.

Ultimately, Dr White’s COVID-19 remedy was never scientifically validated through clinical trials or peer-reviewed research. The Sri Lankan health authorities and the World Health Organization maintained that there was no scientific basis for the efficacy of his concoction. The use of traditional and alternative medicines was discouraged as a substitute for proven preventive measures and treatments.

In summary, while Dr Eliyantha White did develop and promote an alleged COVID-19 medicine and expressed intentions to use it on Navy personnel, there is insufficient evidence of official approval from the Prime Minister for such use. The claim is partially accurate in describing Dr White’s actions and intent but overstates the level of government endorsement and the scientific credibility of the proposed medicine.

article_content:
A widely circulated social media post claims to depict Sri Lankan soldiers and police officers having their meals on the streets during the COVID-19 pandemic. The image attached shows uniformed personnel seated on the pavement, eating from lunch packets, with what appears to be an urban backdrop. The post has gained significant attention online, with many users expressing sympathy and gratitude for the sacrifices made by frontline workers during the pandemic.

To evaluate the authenticity of this claim, it is important to consider the context in which the image was shared, the visual details within the image, and the documented activities of Sri Lankan security forces during the COVID-19 crisis.

Background

Sri Lanka, like many countries, implemented strict measures to curb the spread of COVID-19, including island-wide lockdowns, travel restrictions, and curfews. The military and police were tasked with enforcing these measures, manning checkpoints, and ensuring compliance in both urban and rural areas. Reports from the period highlighted the long hours and challenging conditions faced by these personnel. Images and stories of their efforts were frequently shared on social media, often accompanied by messages of appreciation.

Analysis

Examining the image closely, several indicators align with the claim. The uniforms worn by the individuals appear consistent with those issued to Sri Lankan military and police. The tropical setting, with visible signage and architectural features, is suggestive of a South Asian urban environment, possibly Sri Lankan. The individuals are seated on sidewalks and appear to be eating quickly, which is plausible for frontline workers unable to leave their posts for extended meal breaks.

However, reverse image searches and further scrutiny reveal that similar images have been circulated online since before the COVID-19 pandemic, sometimes in connection with other events such as disaster response efforts or national celebrations. In some instances, such images have been used to highlight the hardships faced by security personnel during various operations, not just during the pandemic.

Fact-Checking

Direct evidence linking this specific image to the COVID-19 pandemic is lacking. While it is plausible that Sri Lankan soldiers and police ate on the streets due to the nature of their duties during the pandemic, the image in question cannot be definitively verified as having been taken during this period. Without clear time-stamping or corroborating reports from that specific time frame, it is possible that the photo was repurposed from earlier events or used out of context.

Furthermore, while multiple credible reports confirm that frontline workers in Sri Lanka operated under difficult conditions during the pandemic—including eating meals in public places or at checkpoints—this particular image does not provide conclusive proof of being from the COVID-19 era.

Conclusion

The core claim—that the image shows Sri Lankan soldiers and police having their meals on the streets during the COVID-19 pandemic—remains unverified. While the scene depicted is plausible and consistent with some experiences of frontline workers during the pandemic, the lack of definitive evidence tying the image to the COVID-19 context means the claim should be treated with caution. The image may still accurately reflect the hardships faced by Sri Lankan security forces, but its specific association with the pandemic cannot be confirmed based on the available information.

متنی که در اینجا ارائه شده است، ادعا را مطرح می‌کند که یک پست محبوب در شبکه‌های اجتماعی به تصویر کشیده است، در آن سربازان و پلیس شری لانکا در طول بحران کرونا در خیابان‌ها غذا می‌خورند. تصویر متصل به این پست، افرادی در لباس‌های نظامی و پلیسی را نشان می‌دهد که روی کناری خیابان نشسته و از حبوبات غذا می‌خورند، در حالی که پس‌زمینه به نظر می‌رسد شهری است. این پست در اینترنت توجه زیادی جذب کرده است و بسیاری از کاربران با احساس شکر و احترام به تلاش‌های کارگران خط جبهه در طول بحران کرونا علاقه‌مندند.

برای ارزیابی واقعیت این ادعا، لازم است با سرچسب اشتراک گذاری تصویر، جزئیات تصویر و فعالیت‌های ثبت شده ارتش و پلیس شری لانکا در طول بحران کرونا، به تحلیل پرداخت.

زمینه

شری لانکا، مانند بسیاری از کشورهای دیگر، اقدامات صریحی را برای کاهش پخش کرونا انجام داد، شامل قرنطینه کامل جزیره، محدودیت‌های تردد و نیروی مسلح و پلیس را برای اجرای این اقدامات، مراقبت از مراقبت‌های گذاری و اطمینان از اجرای دستورات در مناطق شهری و روستایی تعیین کرد. گزارش‌های دوره‌ای نشان داده است که ساعات طولانی و شرایط چالش برانگیزی که این افراد با آن مواجه بودند. تصاویر و داستان‌های تلاش‌های آن‌ها به طور مکرر در شبکه‌های اجتماعی به اشتراک گذاشته می‌شد، اغلب با پیام‌های تشکر و احترام همراه بود.

تحلیل

در نگاهی دقیق به تصویر، چند نشانه با ادعا هماهنگ است. لباس‌هایی که افراد در تصویر پوشیده‌اند، با لباس‌هایی که به نیروی مسلح و پلیس شری لانکا تعلق دارد، هماهنگ است. محیط گرم، با نشانه‌های معمول و ویژگی‌های معماری، به محیط شهری جنوب آسیایی، ممکن است شری لانکا را نشان می‌دهد. افراد در تصویر روی پارکینگ نشسته و به نظر می‌رسد که غذا را سریعاً می‌خورند که این احتمالاً برای کارگران خط جبهه که می‌توانند به مدت طولانی از محل خود باز نشوند، معتبر است.

با این حال، جستجوی تصویر معکوس و بررسی بیشتر نشان می‌دهد که تصاویر مشابه این از قبل از بحران کرونا در اینترنت پخش شده است، گاهی در ارتباط با رویدادهای دیگر مانند پاسخ به بحران یا تجلیل ملی. در برخی مواقع، این تصاویر برای توجه به مشکلاتی که نیروی امنیت در طول عملیات مختلف مواجه شده‌اند، استفاده شده است، نه فقط در طول بحران کرونا.

بررسی واقعیت

دلیل مستقیمی که این تصویر را به بحران کرونا مرتبط می‌کند، وجود ندارد. در حالی که احتمالاً سربازان و پلیس شری لانکا در طول بحران کرونا به دلیل وظایف خود در خیابان غذا می‌خوردند، تصویر در مورد این موضوع به طور قطعی قابل تأیید نیست. بدون زمان‌بندی واضح یا گزارشاتی که از دوره خاصی از زمان مربوط به این تصویر باشد، امکان دارد که این تصویر از رویدادهای قبلی استفاده شده یا در خارج از محتوای خود به کار رفته باشد.

علاوه بر این، هرچند گزارش‌های متعددی وجود دارد که تأکید می‌کنند کارگران خط جبهه در شری لانکا در طول بحران کرونا در شرایط سختی عمل می‌کردند، شامل خوردن غذا در مکان‌های عمومی یا در نقاط گذاری، اما تصویر مورد نظر اثبات قطعی این امر را در دوره کرونا ارائه نمی‌دهد.

نتیجه

اصلی ادعا که تصویر سربازان و پلیس شری لانکا را در خیابان در طول بحران کرونا غذا می‌خورند، هنوز تأیید نشده است. در حالی که صحنه نشان داده شده در تصویر واقعی و هماهنگ با برخی تجربیات کارگران خط جبهه در طول بحران کرونا است، عدم وجود دلیل قطعی ارتباط تصویر با این دوره به معنی این است که این ادعا با احتیاط مورد بررسی قرار گیرد. تصویر ممکن است هنوز به درستی مشکلاتی که نیروی امنیت شری لانکا در طول بحران کرونا مواجه شده‌اند را نشان دهد، اما ارتباط خاص آن با بحران کرونا به دلیل اطلاعات موجود قابل تأیید نیست.
